## Objective
- Build a playable 2D idle RPG combining Melvor Idle-style progression with Godville-style narration, animations, and uncapped offline progress.
- Add meaningful combat and crafting systems to the existing game.

## Requirements
- Build the game, making reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Continue progressing while the player is away with no offline-time cap.
- Add combat and crafting to the existing game.

## Decisions
- The game is “Odd Gods,” a self-contained browser game with localStorage saves and CSS-animated scenes.
- Existing resource gathering, quests, upgrades, humorous narration, and offline gains remain part of the game.

### Completed
- Built the existing game UI and idle progression in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added README play instructions and fixed level calculation and quest progression.
- Previously verified JavaScript syntax and desktop/mobile rendering.

### Active
- Implement combat and crafting gameplay in the existing game; combat currently only operates as a passive “Fight slimes” resource action, and crafting is not implemented.

- (none)

1. Add functional combat progression and crafting recipes/actions to the existing game.
2. Connect their resources, skills, rewards, UI, and saving to current systems.
3. Run syntax and browser checks.

- `game.js`: Game state, actions, idle/offline progress, quests, upgrades, and modals.
- `index.html`: Game layout and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling, animations, and responsive layout.
- `README.md`: Local play instructions.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing resources include herbs, wood, ore, fish, coins, favor, and slime essence; combat currently grants coins and essence but has no enemy or battle mechanics.
- Progress is saved in browser `localStorage`; offline time is uncapped.

## Objective
- Add randomly generated, activity-matched scenes to Odd Gods while preserving gameplay and progression.
- Check scene behavior and rendering on desktop and mobile.

## Requirements
- Scenes must match the selected and saved activity.
- Keep the game self-contained with localStorage saves and CSS-animated scenes.
- Include a “New map” control to reroll the current scene.
- Preserve existing idle and uncapped offline progress.

## Decisions
- Generate scenes from activity-specific biomes, locations, weather, and props.
- Persist scene details with the save so the scene remains consistent.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added activity-specific scene data, saved scene generation, reroll control, matching hero tools, and scene rendering.
- Added biome palette styling and responsive adjustments; hid incongruous scenery in several biomes.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed before the latest CSS and scene-validation edits.

### Active
- Validate scene generation, activity switching, rerolling, and save/load behavior.
- Check desktop and mobile rendering.
- Confirm existing idle and uncapped offline gains remain unchanged.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run syntax and functional checks after the latest edits.
2. Review generated scenes at desktop and mobile sizes; fix any issues.
3. Confirm existing progression and offline gains remain intact.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Activity selection, scene generation/rendering, saved state, and progression.
- `index.html`: Scene markup and map reroll control.
- `style.css`: Biome palettes, scenery, animation, and responsive styling.
- `README.md`: Local play instructions and feature summary.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `README.md` is modified, and `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `style.css` are untracked.
- Existing combat and crafting were previously added and checked; offline progression is in `game.js` (`offline()` and the interval loop).
